items.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Bob Howard and some of those guys were doing it on those local stations.

ctx.x: Well you know the whole…that period that you are describing was a unique period, both in the recording business and it was the embryo time of television. In those days they had staff bands at CBS and NBC and places like that.

Yeah 66 men there was. And it was…time is completely different now. But you see during those times we were making 75 percent of all the recording music made in America. It was made right here in New York City. It practically invented the TV jingle. The jingle was really an invention that came out of New York. Bob Howard and some of those guys were doing it on those local stations. So there was a lot of work. Then we had the three networks each using 66 musicians each and we still had all of the hotels in the…
